However, shipped's sample size annotation N = 40 is demonstrably wrong: 40 is the number of learner texts sampled in the corpus (p. 12), whereas UAM Corpus Tool computed the 2x2 chi-square test on raw obligatory-context token frequencies (p. 18, section 3.3; p. 19, footnotes 7–8), which for progressive -ing are 18/38 (beginners) vs. 44/47 (intermediates), giving a contingency-table total of N = 38 + 47 = 85 (reproducing χ2 = 85*(18*3 - 20*44)^2 / (38*47*62*23) = 22.771). confirmed_errors.location: p. 26, Experiment 5, Results and Discussion; Table 7A
confirmed_errors.reason: In Gick & Holyoak (1983), Experiment 5 (p. 26, Table 7A), the key comparison of producing the convergence solution before the hint between the with-principle condition (62%, 45/73) and the without-principle condition (40%, 28/70) is tested using a maximum-likelihood chi-square test reported as G2(1) = 6.75, p < .01 (exact p = 0.009375). The shipped value (0.01548195) is not from the original paper; it was recalculated in Boyce et al. (2023) using a Yates-corrected Pearson chi-square test on the 2x2 counts (45/73 vs. 28/70, X2(1) = 5.8608, p = 0.01548195). The blind extraction correctly captures the original paper's reported p-value (< .01).

confirmed_errors.location: Results, Confirmatory Analysis, Main analysis: AUC values (lines 268-272)
confirmed_errors.reason: Although 90 participants (47 older and 43 younger adults; also matching the planned sample of 90) passed the initial attention check and demographic screening, 18 participants were excluded from the primary confirmatory analysis of log-transformed AUC donation values due to failed hyperbolic discount curve fitting or outliers exceeding 3 SDs. This left a final analytic sample of 72 participants (37 older, 35 younger), which directly corresponds to the degrees of freedom in the confirmatory ANOVA (F(1, 70)) and post-hoc Welch t-test (t(69.23) = -0.03).

confirmed_errors.location: pp. 518–519, §7.1.1 Participants
